ministry_ne: संस्कृति पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्यन मन्त्रालय
summary:
The main purpose of the Air Services Authority of Nepal Bill, 2083 is to develop modern, well-equipped airport infrastructure in accordance with international standards, as well as a safe and reliable air navigation system in Nepal, to make air services high-quality and effective, and to develop skilled human resources (Explanatory Note, Page 1). This Act shall come into force on the 91st day from the date of certification (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 16).

The Federal Government of Nepal carries responsibilities including granting approval for airport construction and operation (Section 12, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 24), publishing a notice in the Nepal Gazette specifying the four boundaries of the approved airport (Section 12, Subsection 4, Page 24), setting standards for environmental protection, noise, and air pollution around the airport and determining bases for control (Section 18, Page 26), designating the entity to operate aeronautical meteorological information services (Section 27, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 29), managing the security of airports and airport areas (Section 28, Subsection 1, Page 29), and acquiring land or structures according to prevailing law upon request of the Authority to provide them (Section 50, Page 36). A local level may, with the approval of the Authority, construct and operate a helipad in its area according to standards approved by the regulatory body (Section 12, Subsection 5, Page 24). Regarding provincial governments, other responsibilities apart from contributing funds to the Authority's fund are not stated in the bill (Section 37, Subsection 2, Clause f, Page 33).

This bill covers private individuals, air service providers, airlines, and government and non-government entities and businesses operating at airports (Section 12, Subsection 6, Page 24; Section 44, Page 36). Any person may, with the Authority's approval, construct a helipad for private use according to approved standards (Section 12, Subsection 6, Page 24). No person shall establish an unmanaged slaughterhouse or dump garbage within 3 km around an airport area (Section 19, Subsection 3, Page 26). No person shall fly or land an aircraft in Nepal's airspace without obtaining air traffic management permission from the Authority (Section 22, Page 28). Entities providing air navigation services must install equipment and keep it in operational condition (Section 26, Page 29). Entities providing aeronautical meteorological services must coordinate with the Authority, comply with regulatory standards, and establish an information center at each airport (Section 27, Subsection 3 and 4, Page 29). All service providers operating at an airport must prioritize passenger safety and convenience and provide quality services (Section 44, Page 36). The chairperson, members, managing director, employees, and experts of the Authority are prohibited from directly or indirectly participating or becoming stakeholders in any transaction or contract with the Authority (Section 51, Page 37). The Authority may collect delayed fees from any firm, company, or institution that fails to pay prescribed fees or rents within the specified time, or prohibit them from using airport services (Section 21, Subsection 2 and 3, Page 27). If an employee wishes to move to the regulatory body, they must submit an application to the Ministry within 60 days from the date of publication of the notice in the Nepal Gazette by the Government of Nepal (Section 35, Subsection 2, Page 32).

To operate an internal or international airport, one must register with the regulatory body according to prevailing law and obtain an airport operation certificate (Aerodrome Certificate) and renew it, though for specified internal airports, services may be operated by obtaining only a registration certificate (Section 13, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 24). The Authority must obtain a license from the regulatory body to provide air navigation services in Nepal's airspace and must adhere to the prescribed standards and quality (Section 24, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 28). Communication, aeronautical navigation, and surveillance equipment must be maintained in operational condition according to standards (Section 26, Page 29). The Authority must implement a Safety Management System and a Quality Management System (Section 5, Clause c, Subclause 4, Page 19). In addition, standards for airports and helipads must be prepared and submitted to the regulatory body for approval (Section 5, Clause d, Subclause 1, Page 19).

This bill creates the Air Services Authority of Nepal (ASAN), whose central office shall be located in Kathmandu Valley (Section 3, Subsection 1, 2, and 3, Page 18). Its main functions include constructing, upgrading, operating, and managing airport infrastructure, providing air navigation and air traffic services, and operating flight safety, search and rescue, and fire-fighting services (Section 5, Page 18-20). For its governance, a 7-member Board of Directors is formed, consisting of a Chairperson appointed by the Government of Nepal, Joint Secretaries from the Ministry, Ministry of Finance, and Ministry of Home Affairs (3 persons), 2 members nominated by the Government of Nepal including at least 1 woman, and the Managing Director (Section 6, Subsection 1, Page 20). The term of office for the Chairperson and nominated members shall be 4 years, and they may be re-nominated once (Section 6, Subsection 3, Page 21). A person holding at least a Master's degree with 15 years of work experience in civil aviation (including 5 years of managerial experience) selected through open competition shall be appointed as Managing Director for a 4-year term to act as the chief executive (Section 31, Subsection 1 and 5, Page 30-31). The Authority shall have its own separate fund containing service fees, rent, fines, grants, loans, and funds received from the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, or local levels (Section 37, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 33).
title: Air Services Authority of Nepal Bill, 2083
